breakfast.name: Arepa de Huevo (Egg-Stuffed Arepa)
instructions: Mix cornmeal, water, salt to form dough
Shape into thick discs, fry until a crust forms
Remove from oil, carefully crack open a small hole in each
Crack a raw egg into the cavity
Seal the hole with a bit of dough
Return to oil, fry until egg is cooked through and arepa is golden
Drain and eat immediately
breakfast.description: A fried corn cake with a whole egg hidden inside — Cartagena's iconic street breakfast. The trick is frying twice to cook the egg without burning the arepa.

breakfast.name: Changua (Milk and Egg Soup)
instructions: Heat milk and water together
Season with salt and scallion
When simmering, crack eggs directly into the liquid
Poach eggs gently 3-4 min
Add torn stale bread to soak
Garnish with cilantro
Serve in bowls with the poached eggs
breakfast.description: Bogotá's hangover cure — milk soup with poached eggs and stale bread. Simple, restorative, and beloved by bogotanos.

breakfast.name: Calentado (Reheated Leftovers)
instructions: Fry hogao: sauté diced onion and tomato with cumin until soft
Add leftover rice and beans, stir to combine and reheat
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Grill arepa and chorizo
Plate: rice-beans, egg on top, arepa and chorizo on the side
breakfast.description: Yesterday's rice and beans refried with hogao sauce — Colombia's universal breakfast. Better the second time around.

breakfast.name: Changua (Milk and Egg Soup)
instructions: Heat milk and water together until simmering — do not boil hard
Add salt and green onion
Crack eggs directly into the simmering milk — poach them in the milk
The eggs should be just set — runny yolks are traditional
Tear stale bread into chunks and place in bowls
Ladle milky broth and poached eggs over bread
Garnish with cilantro
This is Bogotá's hangover cure and morning ritual — the bread soaks up the milky broth
breakfast.description: Bogotá's breakfast that divides the world — eggs poached in hot milk over stale bread. You either think it sounds bizarre or you become obsessed. Viral videos of Colombians making and defending changua have millions of views because the concept is so unfamiliar outside the Andes.

lunch.name: Bandeja Paisa
instructions: Cook beans with pork hock, cumin, salt until tender
Make hogao: sauté onion and tomato with cumin
Cook ground beef in hogao
Fry chicharrón until crackling and crispy
Fry ripe plantain slices until caramelized
Grill chorizo
Fry egg
Cook rice, warm arepa
Arrange everything on one massive plate — nothing touches if you do it right
Serve with avocado slices
lunch.description: Antioquia's famous platter — literally everything on one plate. A mountain of protein and carbs that defines paisa culture. Not a meal, a monument.

lunch.name: Ajiaco Santafereño
ingredients: 3 types of potato: papa criolla (small yellow, dissolves), papa pastusa (floury), papa sabanera (waxy)
instructions: Boil chicken in salted water with corn, skim foam
After 20 min, add all three types of potato
The papa criolla will dissolve and thicken the soup naturally
Add guascas herb — this is what makes it ajiaco
Cook until chicken is tender, remove, shred, return
The soup should be thick from the dissolved potatoes
Serve in deep bowls with corn, topped with cream, capers, and avocado slices
lunch.description: Bogotá's signature soup — three types of potato, each playing a different role, flavored with the guascas herb found nowhere else. Rain-day food in a rain-day city.

lunch.name: Sancocho de Gallina
instructions: Simmer hen in large pot with garlic, scallion, cumin
Cook 45 min until hen is tender
Add corn, yuca, plantain, potato
Simmer 30 more min until everything is tender
Add chopped cilantro
Serve in big bowls with broth, meat, and vegetables
Eat alongside rice and avocado
lunch.description: The Colombian grandmother's chicken soup — always made with a tough old hen for deeper flavor. Every region has its version; every version is Sunday lunch.

dinner.name: Lechona Tolimense
ingredients: Filling: dried yellow peas (cooked), rice, pork loin (cubed), onion, garlic, cumin, pepper, scallion
instructions: Clean whole pig, debone partially
Cook filling: mix peas, rice, seasoned pork loin
Stuff pig with filling
Sew closed
Roast in wood-fired oven 8-10 hours until skin is crackling and golden
Carve at the table
Serve with arepa — make sure every plate gets crispy skin, filling, and meat
dinner.description: A whole stuffed pig roasted for 10 hours — Tolima's festival dish. The crispy skin (cuerito) is fought over.

dinner.name: Cazuela de Mariscos
ingredients: Mixed seafood: shrimp, squid, fish, clams, crab
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, pepper with achiote and cumin
Add tomato, cook until broken down
Pour in coconut milk, bring to simmer
Add seafood: fish first, then squid, shrimp, clams last
Cook just until seafood is done — do not overcook
Finish with lime and cilantro
Serve with plantain chips
dinner.description: Caribbean coast seafood stew in coconut milk — Cartagena at its most delicious. The Pacific coast version uses different fish but the same soul.

dinner.name: Lomo al Trapo (Cloth-Wrapped Beef)
ingredients: Chimichurri: parsley, garlic, olive oil, vinegar
instructions: Dampen cloth, spread thick layer of coarse salt over it
Place beef tenderloin on salt
Cover completely with more salt — a thick crust
Wrap cloth tightly around salted beef, tie with string
Place directly in hot charcoal embers
Cook 25-30 min, turning once
The cloth chars, the salt forms a hard crust
Break crust open, slice — the meat inside is perfectly pink and seasoned only on the outside
Serve with chimichurri
dinner.description: Beef tenderloin wrapped in cloth and salt, cooked directly in embers — a Colombian gaucho technique. Dramatic and perfectly cooked every time.

snacks.name: Empanadas Colombianas
ingredients: Filling: potatoes (cubed small), shredded beef or pork, hogao, cumin
Ají sauce: cilantro, scallion, lime, chili, vinegar
instructions: Cook filling: mix seasoned meat with potatoes and hogao
Make dough with cornmeal, achiote water (for yellow color)
Form thin patties, fill with mixture
Fold into half-moon, seal edges firmly
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with ají sauce
snacks.description: Crispy cornmeal empanadas — sold on every street corner in Colombia. The yellow comes from achiote. Always eaten with ají.

snacks.name: Buñuelos
instructions: Mix cheese, cornstarch, egg, sugar, baking powder into dough
Shape into ping-pong-sized balls
Deep fry, turning constantly, until golden all around — they puff up
Drain — they should be crispy outside and airy-cheesy inside
snacks.description: Cheese-dough balls fried until puffy and golden — Christmas in Colombia isn't Christmas without buñuelos. The cheese makes them tangy inside.

desserts.name: Tres Leches Cake
ingredients: Cake: 5 eggs, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup flour, vanilla
Soak: 1 can evaporated milk, 1 can condensed milk, 1 cup heavy cream
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until tripled in volume
Fold in flour gently — the air is everything
Bake at 175°C for 25-30 min
Cool completely
Mix three milks together, pour over cake slowly
Refrigerate overnight — the cake absorbs all the milk
Top with whipped cream and cinnamon dust
desserts.description: Sponge cake soaked in three milks — it should be saturated through and spoon-soft. Every bite is milk on milk on milk.

desserts.name: Obleas con Arequipe
instructions: Spread generous arequipe on one wafer
Add coconut, jam if desired
Press another wafer on top
Eat like a sandwich
desserts.description: Two paper-thin wafers sandwiching dulce de leche — sold at parks and plazas across Colombia. Simple and perfect.

drinks.name: Aguapanela con Limón
instructions: Dissolve panela in hot water — it takes stirring
Add lime juice generously
Serve hot (for cold nights) or cold over ice (for hot days)
The hot version is Colombia's cold remedy; the cold version is Colombia's Gatorade
drinks.description: Dissolved raw cane sugar with lime — the most Colombian drink there is. Hot or cold, morning or night, it's everywhere.

drinks.name: Lulada
instructions: Mash lulo fruit by hand — do not blend (texture matters)
Mix with water, sugar, lime juice
Serve over ice with fruit chunks still visible
drinks.description: Cali's signature drink — hand-crushed lulo fruit over ice. The tart, citrusy flavor can't be replicated with any other fruit.
